technical.summary: Extreme overbought conditions across multiple oscillators with bearish stochastic cross and negative CMF undermine bullish trend structure; high risk of pullback despite neutral sector backdrop.

fundamental.summary: AIG shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signals, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and elevated earnings risk within 98 days.

sentiment.summary: Weak sell signal from minor congressional sales 91-98 days ago; neutral market sentiment and unavailable news data provide no confirmation or contradiction.

risk.summary: Severe macro deterioration with inverted yield curve, crisis-level VIX (291.36), falling dollar, imminent CPI event, and negative macro score (-6) create hostile environment for financials; earnings 98 days out provides minimal near-term relief.

debate.key_bull_argument: RSI 14 rising with supertrend bullish and price above Ichimoku cloud provide structural uptrend confirmation despite overbought conditions.
debate.key_bear_argument: Extreme overbought oscillators (RSI 9/14, Stochastic, Williams %R), bearish stochastic cross, negative CMF, crisis-level VIX, inverted yield curve, and zero fundamental/insider support create compounding pullback risk in hostile macro environment.

decision.entry_rationale: RSI 14 rising with supertrend bullish and Ichimoku cloud support suggest structural uptrend, but entry quality is severely compromised by extreme overbought conditions and hostile macro backdrop.
decision.primary_risk: Crisis-level VIX (291.36), inverted yield curve, and extreme overbought oscillators create imminent pullback risk; bearish stochastic cross and negative CMF signal momentum exhaustion despite price structure.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding AIG with 84 existing Financials positions (27% of portfolio); sector concentration and existing ticker exposure demand conviction threshold >60 for new entry; current 18-point score falls far short.
